A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe DDP-WM and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1-10, Figures 1-9 and Appendices A-I. Textual and visual inspection supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated planning, efficiency and ablation results in Section 4, plus PCA and qualitative rollout analyses in Appendices A and I.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including planning performance across five simulated environments, component ablations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The four-stage architecture, sparse MPC cost mask, CEM procedure, adaptive sparse sizing and staged training remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices D, E and H.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PointMaze, Wall, Push-T, Rope and Granular under the same task coverage. Appendix I retains the same Push-T, Granular and Rope rollout examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains IRIS, DreamerV3, Sparse Imagination and DINO-WM with identical task participation. The comparison methods and component variants in the other experiments also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, MPC and efficiency protocols, and model/training settings are unchanged. Appendix F retains five-step rollouts on 400 validation episodes using the same frozen-decoder procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same LRM, MPC-mask and localization ablations, optimization-landscape analysis, background-update PCA and qualitative rollout analyses in Section 4 and Appendices A and I.

E5.justification: Appendix F retains the fixed-random-seed statement, and Figure 6 retains mean curves with one-standard-deviation bands. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, both versions report Push-T success rates of 98% for DDP-WM and 90% for DINO-WM, and throughput of 1563 versus 170 samples/second.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, low-rank background-update assumption and Gram-matrix characterization, equations (1)-(5), and mathematical reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about disentangled dynamics, LRM-enabled planning, and improved performance and efficiency. No contribution is added, removed or substantively strengthened.

C2.justification: The explanations linking feature consistency to planner smoothness, the staged-training rationale in Appendix H, and the granular-prediction failure discussion in Appendix I.2 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from a future code-release promise with a repository address to a current availability statement with a clickable project-site link. Implementation, hardware and hyperparameter documentation otherwise remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B and the reference list are unchanged, including positioning against DINO-WM, Sparse Imagination and object-centric world models.

P1.justification: v4 adds X-Era AI Lab affiliations for Yang Liu and Liang Lin, updates dates and the code sentence, and introduces stray question marks into Section 4.4.1 references to Appendix F and Table 6. Section structure and scientific prose otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Limited reflow affects the abstract, affiliation footnote and Section 4.4.1 text, while the project address gains hyperlink formatting. Figures and tables retain their content, organization and placement.

improvement.justification: Scientific content and empirical evidence are unchanged. The new code-availability statement and project link could improve reproducibility, but the PDFs do not establish the hosted resources, and the introduction still promises future release. Meanwhile, v4 introduces malformed Appendix F and Table 6 references. These mixed documentation changes do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
